content: 1. Uncertainty in Valuing Outcomes: There is possibly important uncertainty or variability in how much individuals value the primary outcomes of the intervention. 2. Resource Requirements: The resource requirements for the intervention are judged to involve moderate costs. 3. Cost-Effectiveness: The cost-effectiveness of the intervention does not favor either the intervention or the comparison. 4. Impact on Health Equity: The intervention is judged to probably have no impact on health equity. 5. Acceptability: The intervention is considered acceptable to key stakeholders. 6. Feasibility: The intervention is deemed feasible to implement. 7. Summary of Findings: The assessment focused on the self-management of medical abortion compared to provider assessment for outcomes of abortion in individuals undergoing medical abortion at less than 12 weeks of gestation. The intervention involved self-assessment of abortion outcomes, while the comparison involved provider assessment. The proportion of individuals assessed to have a successful abortion was 940 per 1,000 in both groups, with a relative risk (RR) of 1.53 (95% confidence interval: 922 to 969). This evidence is based on one randomized controlled trial (RCT) with 700 participants and is rated as low certainty due to broad confidence intervals. Cost data, including comparative costs and costs to the patient, were not reported. 8. Evidence Limitations: The certainty of evidence was downgraded due to broad confidence intervals and heterogeneity. Lack of blinding may have influenced the outcomes. Findings from different studies varied: Oppgaard et al. (Nordic countries) reported a preference for self-management, while Iyengar et al. (India) reported satisfaction with follow-up methods. 9. References: Oppgaard et al. conducted a multicenter, non-inferiority randomized controlled trial comparing clinical follow-up with self-assessment after medical abortion (Lancet, 2015). Iyengar et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial in India comparing self-assessment with clinic follow-up for early medical abortion outcomes (Lancet Global Health, 2015). Mählck and Bäckström compared clinical assessment with self-assessment in a rural hospital in northern Norway (Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol, 2017).
